android_mechanism: Repeated lookup executed per row during import; fix caches the lookup
bug_description: In the playlist page content list, every song row build passes sid/index to SongCard as this.list.indexOf(item), twice per row. indexOf is a linear scan over the whole (potentially 1000+) song list, so rendering/scrolling the playlist costs O(n) per row and O(n^2) cumulative, wasting UI-thread time as the list grows.
fix_summary: The index already provided by the LazyForEach item generator is passed to SongCard, removing both per-row linear scans.
trigger_steps: Log in or use a playlist with 500+ songs; open the playlist detail page.
Start hitrace capture (categories: ace, app, sched).
Scroll the song list from top to bottom at constant speed.
Stop hitrace. Repeat 3 repetitions for unfixed, then install the fixed HAP and repeat 3 repetitions.

test_oracle.definition: UI-thread CPU time attributable to list-row building during the scroll (from ace trace component-build events), divided by number of rows rendered.
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed per-row build time grows linearly with playlist size (indexOf scan) while fixed stays constant; with >= 500 songs, unfixed scroll CPU > fixed by >= 10% and unfixed shows more dropped frames.

trace_config.command: hdc shell hitrace --time 25 ace app sched graphic -o /data/local/tmp/cm_indexof.chtrace
